cim_eredeti: Figure 03 robot passes Elon Musk's apple test, adapts when table moved
szoveg_eredeti:
Figure 03 retrieved an apple after a person moved the table, responding to Musk's criticism of humanoid demos.

Adcock called the demonstration "zero shot and fully autonomous," using Figure's Helix AI system.

Figure's Helix 2.5 completed 56 percent of household chore trials across 30 previously unseen homes.

Figure AI CEO Brett Adcock has responded to Elon Musk’s criticism of humanoid robot demonstrations with a video showing a Figure 03 robot picking up an apple after the table beneath it is moved. The 41-second clip shows the robot placing the apple back on the table before retrieving it again from its new position.

Musk had argued that humanoid robot demonstrations are often staged and pre-programmed, suggesting that machines cannot reliably adapt when their surroundings change.

Adcock shared the video on November 23, describing the demonstration as “zero shot and fully autonomous,” directly addressing Musk’s apple-picking example.

Adcock responded to Elon Musk’s claim that humanoid robot demonstrations are staged and pre-programmed by sharing a video of a Figure 03 robot retrieving an apple after someone moved the table beneath it.

The 41-second clip shows the humanoid picking up an apple from a table, putting it back, and then retrieving it again after a person moves the table away from its original position. Adcock described the demonstration as “zero shot and fully autonomous,” directly addressing an example Musk had used to question the capabilities of humanoid robots.

"If you ask, "Go pick up an apple," and then you move the table, it won't be able to pick up the apple anymore"Here's Figure running Helix, zero shot and fully autonomous https://t.co/H8BjJBHdFt pic.twitter.com/MMwbnmFjT3

Musk said humanoid robot demonstrations seen so far are generally staged and pre-programmed rather than genuine examples of autonomous operation. He argued that existing robots cannot reliably perform arbitrary tasks involving objects or situations they have never encountered before. For example, he suggested that a robot instructed to pick up an apple would fail if someone moved the table the fruit was sitting on. Musk added that a robot should at least be able to figure out where the apple went after the table was moved.

Musk also said Tesla was making progress with its Optimus humanoid robot and expected to demonstrate a version capable of performing tasks without staging or pre-programmed movements.

The company could hold what he described as an “authentic” demonstration in “a month or two.” Musk said the presentation would offer a better indication of what people could expect when interacting with Optimus in everyday situations.

Adcock responded on November 23 by sharing a video of Figure 03 operating its Helix artificial intelligence system. In the demonstration, a person asks the robot to pick up an apple from a table. After completing the task, the robot is asked to retrieve the fruit again following the table’s movement.

Figure 03 approaches the relocated table and successfully picks up the apple. In Figure’s terminology, zero-shot performance means the robot has not been trained specifically on the particular scene or object. However, this does not mean the underlying tasks themselves were entirely unfamiliar to the system.

Figure’s Helix 2.5 home trials offer a broader indication of the technology’s current capabilities. The company reported that its robots completed 237 of 420 trials, or approximately 56 percent, involving household chores across 30 previously unseen homes. The tasks included making beds, folding towels, and tidying toys.

The results also illustrate the distinction between adapting to an unfamiliar environment and reliably performing arbitrary tasks in the real world.

Figure has previously faced questions about whether its robots operate autonomously. Following criticism of a demonstration featured on the Shawn Ryan Show in April, Adcock defended the company’s autonomy claims. In May, Figure livestreamed an eight-hour, unedited Figure 03 shift involving package sorting.

Meanwhile, Tesla’s earlier Optimus demonstrations have also attracted scrutiny. At the October 2024 We, Robot event, humanoids served drinks and interacted with guests, although human operators assisted them remotely. Tesla did not explain that assistance during the presentation. The company subsequently released videos in May 2025 showing Optimus performing household chores using a neural network it said had learned from human demonstrations.

According to analysts, if Musk’s proposed timeline holds, Tesla could present its latest Optimus demonstration around January 2027. The company has also targeted the end of 2027 for its first customer deliveries of the humanoid robot.

cim: Elon Musk bírálatára válaszolva autonóm módon reagált a Figure robot
lead: A Figure AI egy [videóval](https://t.co/H8BjJBHdFt) bizonyítja, hogy Figure 03 humanoid robotja képes elmozdított környezetben is megtalálni és felvenni a kiszemelt almát.
osszefoglalo:
Brett Adcock, a Figure AI vezérigazgatója egy videóval válaszolt Elon Musk azon bírálatára, miszerint a jelenlegi humanoid robotok bemutatói mind előre programozott jelenetek. Musk szerint egy átlagos robot kudarcot vall, ha a feladat közben elmozdítják az asztalt, amin a tárgy található. A Figure friss tesztjében a **Figure 03** modell a Helix AI segítségével a megváltoztatott helyszínen is sikeresen felvette az almát.

A vállalat közlése szerint a bemutató teljesen autonóm és **zero-shot** módon zajlott, ami azt jelenti, hogy a robotot nem képezték ki előre arra a konkrét helyszínre vagy elrendezésre. A cég korábbi Helix 2.5-ös tesztjei során 30 teljesen ismeretlen otthonban 420 mindennapi feladatból 237-et, vagyis mintegy 56 százalékot tudtak sikeresen elvégezni a robotok.

A humanoid robotok autonómiáját korábban sok kritika érte, mivel a Tesla Optimus bemutatóin is előfordult, hogy emberi operátorok távolról segítették az eszközöket. A Figure a korábbi vádakra válaszul már májusban közzétett egy 8 órás, vágatlan élő közvetítést is a robotok csomagválogatási munkájáról.
miert_szamit: A teszt azt mutatja, hogy a **humanoid robotok** egyre közelebb kerülnek a valódi, dinamikus környezetben történő autonóm munkavégzéshez, ami hosszú távon átírhatja a logisztika és a fizikai munkák automatizálását.
video_szoveg: A videón a Figure 03 robot felvesz egy almát az asztalról, majd miután egy ember elmozdítja az asztalt, a robot követi azt és újra sikeresen megfogja a gyümölcsöt.

prioritas.indok: Bulvár-tech válogatás: 82 pont. Látványos videós robotdemó, ahol a humanoid robot visszavág Elon Musk kritikájára.

prioritas.lead_hu: A Figure AI videóban mutatta be, hogy legújabb robotjuk az asztal elmozdítása után is sikeresen felvette az almát. A demonstrációval Elon Musk korábbi bírálataira válaszoltak.

tenyellenorzes.esemeny: Brett Adcock, a Figure AI vezérigazgatója egy videót tett közzé az X-en, amin a Figure 03 robot teljesen autonóm módon veszi fel az almát az elmozdított asztalról, így reagálva Elon Musk korábbi bírálatára.
